<reason>B won the live clash by granting A’s strongest last-copy/deadline case and still showing that uniqueness explains why to seek consent, not why to override it. A’s archive and future-descendant framing was sharp but never named a legitimate override authority or escaped the no-endpoint problem. B made the proposition easier to decide: once recipients are identified, refusal must actually be able to stop the study.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Rebuttal 2: a hard stop still does not justify the override, and if unread unique evidence required another pause when the deadline arrived, the exception would never end.</best_rebuttal>
